explanation: Musicians in Trinidad began turning discarded oil drums into tuned pans in the 1930s and 1940s. Each note is a separately hammered patch of the drum's top.

claims.text: The steelpan was developed in Trinidad and Tobago.
The steelpan was not developed in Antigua and Barbuda, Jamaica or Barbados.
Trinidadian musicians began making tuned pans from discarded oil drums in the 1930s and 1940s.
Each note of a steelpan is played on its own separately hammered and tuned area of the drum's surface.
